question: What national default school-zone speed limit must every jurisdiction post, regardless of local law or engineering study?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not establish any national default school-zone speed limit, and the evidence provided contains no such value. School speed limits are established either by an engineering study or by statute in each jurisdiction — not by a uniform national number — so the premise of the question is incorrect. Standards (mandatory): - "A School Speed Limit assembly (see Figure 7B-1) or a School Speed Limit When Flashing (S5-1) sign (see Figure 7B-1) shall be used to indicate the speed limit where a reduced school speed limit zone has been established based upon an engineering study or where a reduced school speed limit is specified for such areas by statute." - "The Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (see Figure 2B-3) shall display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study. The speed limits displayed shall be in multiples of 5 mph." - "Speed zones (other than statutory speed limits) shall only be established on the basis of an engineering study that has been performed in accordance with traffic engineering practices. The engineering study shall consider the roadway context." Citations: - Section 7B.05 Standard §1 (p.978) - Section 2B.21 Standard §13 (p.85) - Section 2B.21 Standard §6 (p.84)
